The route gate is where polished assurance meets wet bark, old stone, and a forest that has not signed anything. The route gate is bureaucracy wedged between trees: a tiny official station trying to impose straight lines on a forest that only understands curves. The place breaks into usable table spaces: Queue lane: Wagons line up between rope posts and roots. Stamp shed: A cramped shed holds ledgers, lanterns, and a desk built around a branch. Bypass deer path: A narrow animal trail skirts the official lane. Inspection stump: A huge cut stump has become the inspection counter. Plants and materials: roots buckle the queue stones, moss softens every official post, vines steal loose paper overnight. Animals and...

Block4: The place changes even if the PCs stand still. Local people, creatures, weather, signage, and ward behavior all keep moving around the scene. The gate can log passage or tampering. Taking the official path may be faster but less informed. Ignoring old bypass signs can cost leverage later. A lantern clicks on after the party has already passed. The route bell rings once with no wind. The old bypass looks freshly used. Let the place be funny through overconfident signage, awkward forms, stubborn local habits, and magic that refuses corporate language.
